newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - The sovereigns keep coming.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - The sovereigns keep coming.

text.p: The pound sterling market will be the next stop on the Eurobond circuit for the Republic of Brazil, which has lost its reputation as a shy participant in foreign debt markets.
Late last week, the Central Bank announced it would issue a 150-200 million pound sterling Eurobond via Barclays de Zoete Wedd and CS First Boston in early July.

At the same time, the bank said plans for a Euroyen issue would be put on hold so as not to interfere with Petrobras' 30 billion six-year samurai bond, which is being launched via Daiwa sometime in July.
Some spread talk on the sterling bond has it pricing tighter than the 10-year Argentine level, now at 270 bp over U.K. gilts.
The sterling bond will follow a $3.0 billion 30-year global bond ZYDC - of which $750 million was sold for cash and the rest swapped for Brady bonds - and a 500 billion 20-year Eurolira.
Brazil has also issued in Deutsche mark, Austrian schilling, Dutch Guilder and French franc this year.
The flurry of new paper contrasts sharply with last year, when the Republic of Brazil was far behind Argentina and Mexico in debt issuance.
THE PRIMARY MARKET will be quiet for the first time in three weeks, as far as Brazilian names are concerned.
There is a chance Banco America do Sul could price its $50 million three-year bond with spread talk in the 250 bp range.

Aside from that, no other issues were expected before July, when the Brazilian debt pipeline should flow with plenty of new issues, including bonds from Eletrobras, Petrobras, the Republic of Brazil and Banco BMG.
IN SECONDARY TRADE, new issues widened 10 bp on average because of oversupply, traders said.

"We had $2.5 billion in new paper the past three weeks so it's good that it will be slow this week. That will give the market some time to absorb all this paper," said one Eurobond trader at an international investment bank in Brazil.

* CSN's 10-year bullet ZYJJ was trading at 285 bp, 10 bp wider than its launch price. The $600 million bond was the largest ever issued by a private Brazilian corporate. It took that distincton away from Grupo Votorantim's eight-year putable bond ZYHB, which was issued the week before.
* Cesp's 9.125 percent 10-year bond ZYGZ, which priced at 280 bp and quickly tightened 20 bp, was trading at 290 bp. Traders said the bond was attractive at that spread.
